'''''Crocus nudiflorus''''' is a [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the [[genus]] ''[[Crocus]]'' of the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] Iridaceae. It is an autumn-flowering, dwarf, [[deciduous]] [[perennial plant|perennial]] found in western Europe from southwestern [[France]] to [[Spain]]. It has been cultivated since [[Tudor period|Tudor times]] in [[Great Britain]],<ref name=Jarvis/> where it is now [[naturalized]].<ref name="pacific">{{cite web |title=Pacific Bulb Society {{!}} Fall Blooming Crocus Two |url=https://www.pacificbulbsociety.org/pbswiki/index.php/FallBloomingCrocusTwo |website=www.pacificbulbsociety.org |accessdate=18 June 2020}}</ref>

==Description==
''Crocus nudiflorus'' grows from [[corm]]s,<ref name="rhs">{{cite web |title=Crocus nudiflorus, autumn crocus/RHS Gardening |url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/4912/Crocus-nudiflorus/Details |publisher=rhs.org.uk |accessdate=18 June 2020}}</ref> which spread out into clumps of plants by [[stolons]].<ref name="pacific"/> Each corm usually sends out one long-tubed,<ref name="rhs"/> goblet-shaped,<ref name="pacific"/> or bell-shaped flower.<ref name=Alonso>José Luis Benito Alonso {{google books|rxZHAwAAQBAJ|Wild Flowers of Ordesa and Monte Perdido National Park (Spanish Pyrenees) 2014|page=38}}</ref> The bloom appears in autumn,<ref name="rhs"/> or at the end of summer.<ref name=Alonso/> The colour ranges from deep purple to lilac-purple with a paler throat and bright orange or yellow stigma.<ref name="rhs"/><ref name=Alonso/><ref name="pacific"/> The linear, basal leaves,<ref name="rhs"/> usually with a silvery central stripe,<ref name="pacific"/> are produced in winter and spring following the autumn flowers,<ref name="rhs"/> when the fruits appear.<ref name=Alonso/>

==Taxonomy==
The Latin [[Binomial nomenclature|specific epithet]] ''nudiflorus'' means 'naked flower', in reference to the flower emerging before the leaves.<ref name=Alonso/><ref name=Jarvis>Dr. Peter Jarvis {{google books|5STMDwAAQBAJ|The Pelagic Dictionary of Natural History of the British Isles (2020)|page=686}}</ref>

It was published and described by [[James Edward Smith (botanist)|James Edward Smith]] in 'English Botany' Volume 7 on table 491 in 1798.<ref name="plantlist"/><ref>{{cite web |title=Crocus nudiflorus {{!}} International Plant Names Index |url=https://www.ipni.org/n/436634-1 |publisher=ipni.org ([[International Plant Names Index]]) |accessdate=18 June 2020}}</ref>

==Distribution and habitat==
''Crocus nudiflorus'' is [[native plant|native]] to southwestern [[France]] and [[Spain]].<ref name="pacific"/><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://apps.kew.org/wcsp/namedetail.do?name_id=327378|title=World Checklist of Selected Plant Families: Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew|website=apps.kew.org|access-date=2016-08-12}}</ref>

==Habitat==
It is found on roadsides, meadows and pastures.<ref name=Jarvis/><ref name="pacific"/> It often grows in pastures with other crocus species including ''Crocus vernus'' subsp. ''albiflorus'', but it is often eaten by [[wild boar]]s.<ref name=Alonso/>

==Uses==
It has been used in [[folk medicine]] as an anti-spasmodic, as an abortive and a sedative.<ref name=Alonso/>

==Culture==
In 2002, it was voted by the public as the [[County flowers of the United Kingdom|county flower]] of [[Nottinghamshire]].<ref name=Jarvis/><ref name=plantlife>{{cite web |title=Autumn Crocus |url=https://www.plantlife.org.uk/uk/discover-wild-plants-nature/plant-fungi-species/autumn-crocus |website=Plantlife |accessdate=17 June 2020 |language=en}}</ref>
